results.title: Suspended almost half of the evictions scheduled in Barcelona in the last month
results.description: A key week for the movement in defense of the right to housing, which after forcing early elections is heading towards the first general strike in the State since 2012. The catalyst for all this social effervescence has been the eviction of Maricarmen Abascal and the housing decrees that preceded it. Congress rejected them in the first instance and they were finally approved by the permanent deputation of the Spanish parliamentary chamber. As ARA has learned, since they came into force a month ago, the courts have suspended 129 evictions in Barcelona, that is, practically half of those that were scheduled in the Catalan capital in the last thirty days. In the vast majority of cases, this is due to the direct application of the new decree, which broadly speaking temporarily suspends evictions of vulnerable people without alternative housing so that a case like that of this 87-year-old neighbor from Madrid, who died two weeks after being evicted, is not repeated.
